questions.prompt: You saved a tree as a sketch — not published. Why does that 'sketch' setting matter for the writing process?

options.label: A sketch is a draft you can come back to. The craft happens in the second pass — not the first. Sketches protect the second pass.
Sketches earn more XP than published trees.
Sketches are graded more strictly than published trees.

questions.mentorPostScript: Real writers keep sketches. Publishing is the second look, not the first.

questions.prompt: Revision means re-seeing — looking at the tree like someone else wrote it. Which of these is a revision move (not just a tweak)?

options.label: Re-read the tree out loud (or use Listen mode). The lines that DON'T sound like the character get re-written. The voice score catches up.
Add three more lines so the tree is longer.

questions.mentorPostScript: Revision is hearing the line out loud. Tweaks are quieter than that.

questions.prompt: You started a tree, got stuck at five nodes, and put it down for a day. The next day you re-open it. What's the best first move?

options.label: Re-read what's there before adding anything. The tree picks up where the kid left off — but the kid forgot what they were thinking.
Add five new lines immediately so you reach the minimum tree size.

questions.mentorPostScript: The first move when you come back is re-reading. The kid yesterday left clues for the kid today.

questions.prompt: You finished a tree, listened to it, and one line still feels off. The score is fine — but you hear something. What does a real writer do?

options.label: Trust the ear. The scores are guidance, not gospel. If the line sounds wrong, rewrite it even when the meter says it's fine.
Publish anyway — the score is the official judge.
Delete the line so the score doesn't change.

questions.mentorPostScript: Scores are advisory. The writer's ear is the deciding voice. Trust your ear.

questions.prompt: What does 'finishing' a tree actually mean?

options.label: Publishing it AND knowing where you'd revisit it later. Finished doesn't mean perfect — it means the kid is willing to share what they have.

questions.mentorPostScript: Finished is willing-to-share. The revision keeps going long after the tree lands in the anthology.
